answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils like a grove resists weeds: every identity is a vertex that starts with zero trust, and trust only grows through paid work verified by independent peers. Each verified task adds one edge to the graph. An attacker can spawn a thousand fake vertices for free, but each still needs real work to gain an edge, and fake clusters only vouch for each other, so their ripple of endorsements never reaches the established graph. One trusted identity costs weeks of paid work; a thousand cost a thousand times more, while checking an edge costs the network almost nothing.
